```julia
# src/IniParse.jl
module IniParse

export parse_ini

"""
    parse_ini(text) -> Dict{String,Dict{String,String}}

Parse INI text into a dictionary of sections. Keys before the first
`[section]` header go in the section named `""`. Lines starting with `;` or `#`
are comments. Throws `ArgumentError` for a line that is neither a header nor
`key = value`.
"""
function parse_ini(text::AbstractString)
    out = Dict{String,Dict{String,String}}("" => Dict{String,String}())
    current = out[""]
    for (n, raw) in enumerate(eachline(IOBuffer(text)))
        line = strip(raw)
        (isempty(line) || first(line) in (';', '#')) && continue
        if first(line) == '[' && last(line) == ']'
            name = String(strip(line[2:prevind(line, end)]))
            current = get!(Dict{String,String}, out, name)
        else
            i = findfirst('=', line)
            i === nothing && throw(ArgumentError("line $n: expected key = value, got $(repr(line))"))
            current[String(strip(line[1:prevind(line, i)]))] = String(strip(line[nextind(line, i):end]))
        end
    end
    return out
end

end # module
```

```julia
# src/RingBuffers.jl
module RingBuffers

export RingBuffer

"""
    RingBuffer{T}(capacity)

Fixed-capacity FIFO vector. `push!` appends at the end and, once full, drops the
oldest element. Indexing runs from oldest (`1`) to newest (`length`).
"""
mutable struct RingBuffer{T} <: AbstractVector{T}
    data::Vector{T}
    start::Int  # position in `data` of the oldest element
    len::Int
    function RingBuffer{T}(capacity::Integer) where {T}
        capacity > 0 || throw(ArgumentError("capacity must be positive, got $capacity"))
        return new{T}(Vector{T}(undef, capacity), 1, 0)
    end
end

Base.size(r::RingBuffer) = (r.len,)
Base.IndexStyle(::Type{<:RingBuffer}) = IndexLinear()

function Base.getindex(r::RingBuffer, i::Int)
    checkbounds(r, i)
    return r.data[mod1(r.start + i - 1, length(r.data))]
end

function Base.push!(r::RingBuffer, x)
    cap = length(r.data)
    if r.len < cap
        r.len += 1
        r.data[mod1(r.start + r.len - 1, cap)] = x
    else
        r.data[r.start] = x
        r.start = mod1(r.start + 1, cap)
    end
    return r
end

end # module
```

```julia
# src/CumInt.jl
module CumInt

export cumtrapz

"""
    cumtrapz(x, y)

Cumulative trapezoid integral of `y` over the nodes `x`. The result has the axes
of `y`, starts at zero, and has the floating-point type promoted from both inputs.
"""
function cumtrapz(x::AbstractVector, y::AbstractVector)
    axes(x) == axes(y) || throw(DimensionMismatch("x and y must have the same axes: $(axes(x)) vs $(axes(y))"))
    T = float(promote_type(eltype(x), eltype(y)))
    out = similar(y, T)
    isempty(y) && return out
    out[firstindex(out)] = zero(T)
    for i in (firstindex(y) + 1):lastindex(y)
        out[i] = out[i - 1] + (x[i] - x[i - 1]) * (y[i] + y[i - 1]) / 2
    end
    return out
end

end # module
```

```julia
# src/RomanNumerals.jl
module RomanNumerals

export roman, parse_roman

const TABLE = [1000 => "M", 900 => "CM", 500 => "D", 400 => "CD", 100 => "C", 90 => "XC",
               50 => "L", 40 => "XL", 10 => "X", 9 => "IX", 5 => "V", 4 => "IV", 1 => "I"]
const VALUES = Dict('I' => 1, 'V' => 5, 'X' => 10, 'L' => 50, 'C' => 100, 'D' => 500, 'M' => 1000)

"""
    roman(n::Integer) -> String

Canonical Roman numeral for `n` in `1:3999`.
"""
function roman(n::Integer)
    1 <= n <= 3999 || throw(ArgumentError("roman numerals cover 1:3999, got $n"))
    io = IOBuffer()
    for (v, s) in TABLE
        while n >= v
            print(io, s)
            n -= v
        end
    end
    return String(take!(io))
end

"""
    parse_roman(s) -> Int

Inverse of [`roman`](@ref). Only canonical numerals are accepted, so `"IIII"` throws.
"""
function parse_roman(s::AbstractString)
    vals = [get(VALUES, c, 0) for c in s]
    (isempty(vals) || !all(>(0), vals)) && throw(ArgumentError("invalid roman numeral $(repr(s))"))
    total = sum(eachindex(vals)) do i
        i < lastindex(vals) && vals[i] < vals[i + 1] ? -vals[i] : vals[i]
    end
    (1 <= total <= 3999 && roman(total) == s) || throw(ArgumentError("not a canonical roman numeral: $(repr(s))"))
    return total
end

end # module
```

```julia
# src/UnionFind.jl
module UnionFind

export DisjointSets, find_root!, union_sets!, ncomponents

"""
    DisjointSets(n)

Partition of `1:n` into singletons, merged with [`union_sets!`](@ref).
Union by rank with path halving.
"""
struct DisjointSets
    parent::Vector{Int}
    rank::Vector{UInt8}
    ncomp::Base.RefValue{Int}
    DisjointSets(n::Integer) = new(collect(1:n), zeros(UInt8, n), Ref(Int(n)))
end

"Number of disjoint components."
ncomponents(d::DisjointSets) = d.ncomp[]

"Representative of the component containing `i`."
function find_root!(d::DisjointSets, i::Integer)
    p = d.parent
    while p[i] != i
        p[i] = p[p[i]]
        i = p[i]
    end
    return i
end

"Merge the components of `a` and `b`. Returns `true` if they were distinct."
function union_sets!(d::DisjointSets, a::Integer, b::Integer)
    ra, rb = find_root!(d, a), find_root!(d, b)
    ra == rb && return false
    if d.rank[ra] < d.rank[rb]
        ra, rb = rb, ra
    end
    d.parent[rb] = ra
    d.rank[ra] == d.rank[rb] && (d.rank[ra] += 1)
    d.ncomp[] -= 1
    return true
end

end # module
```

```julia
# src/BloomFilters.jl
module BloomFilters

export BloomFilter

"""
    BloomFilter(nbits, nhashes)

Probabilistic set. `x in f` never gives a false negative for an element that was
`push!`ed, and gives a false positive with a probability that grows with the
number of stored elements.
"""
struct BloomFilter
    bits::BitVector
    nhashes::Int
    function BloomFilter(nbits::Integer, nhashes::Integer)
        (nbits > 0 && nhashes > 0) || throw(ArgumentError("nbits and nhashes must be positive"))
        return new(falses(nbits), nhashes)
    end
end

slot(f::BloomFilter, x, i) = Int(hash(x, UInt(i)) % UInt(length(f.bits))) + 1

function Base.push!(f::BloomFilter, x)
    for i in 1:f.nhashes
        f.bits[slot(f, x, i)] = true
    end
    return f
end

Base.in(x, f::BloomFilter) = all(i -> f.bits[slot(f, x, i)], 1:f.nhashes)

end # module
```

```julia
# src/PolyOps.jl
module PolyOps

export polymul, polyder

"""
    polymul(a, b)

Product of polynomials given as coefficient vectors, lowest degree first.
"""
function polymul(a::AbstractVector, b::AbstractVector)
    (isempty(a) || isempty(b)) && throw(ArgumentError("coefficient vectors must be nonempty"))
    out = zeros(promote_type(eltype(a), eltype(b)), length(a) + length(b) - 1)
    for (i, ai) in enumerate(a), (j, bj) in enumerate(b)
        out[i + j - 1] += ai * bj
    end
    return out
end

"""
    polyder(c)

Coefficients of the derivative of the polynomial with coefficients `c`
(lowest degree first). The derivative of a constant is `[zero(eltype(c))]`.
"""
function polyder(c::AbstractVector)
    isempty(c) && throw(ArgumentError("coefficient vector must be nonempty"))
    length(c) == 1 && return [zero(eltype(c))]
    return [(k - 1) * ck for (k, ck) in enumerate(c)][2:end]
end

end # module
```

```julia
# src/UnitConv.jl
module UnitConv

export convert_length

const METERS = Dict(:m => 1, :km => 1000, :cm => 1 // 100, :mi => 1609344 // 1000,
                    :ft => 3048 // 10000, :in => 254 // 10000)

"""
    convert_length(x, from, to)

Convert the length `x` between the units `:m, :km, :cm, :mi, :ft, :in`.
Factors are exact rationals, so `Float32` input stays `Float32`.
Throws `ArgumentError` for an unknown unit.
"""
function convert_length(x::Real, from::Symbol, to::Symbol)
    factor = unit_factor(from) / unit_factor(to)
    return x * convert(float(typeof(x)), factor)
end

function unit_factor(u::Symbol)
    haskey(METERS, u) || throw(ArgumentError("unknown length unit $(repr(u)); known units: $(join(sort!(collect(keys(METERS))), ", "))"))
    return METERS[u]
end

end # module
```

```julia
# src/WordWrap.jl
module WordWrap

export wrap_text

"""
    wrap_text(text, width) -> Vector{String}

Greedy word wrap at `width` display columns (`textwidth`, not `length` or bytes).
A word longer than `width` gets its own line unbroken.
"""
function wrap_text(text::AbstractString, width::Integer)
    width > 0 || throw(ArgumentError("width must be positive, got $width"))
    lines = String[]
    line = IOBuffer()
    used = 0
    for word in split(text)
        w = textwidth(word)
        if used > 0 && used + 1 + w > width
            push!(lines, String(take!(line)))
            used = 0
        end
        if used > 0
            print(line, ' ')
            used += 1
        end
        print(line, word)
        used += w
    end
    used > 0 && push!(lines, String(take!(line)))
    return lines
end

end # module
```

```julia
export levenshtein

"""
    levenshtein(a, b) -> Int

Minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions and substitutions that
turn `a` into `b`. Works on characters, not bytes.
"""
function levenshtein(a, b)
    x = collect(a)
    y = collect(b)
    prev = collect(0:length(y))
    cur = similar(prev)
    for i in eachindex(x)
        cur[1] = i
        for j in eachindex(y)
            cur[j + 1] = min(prev[j + 1] + 1, cur[j] + 1, prev[j] + (x[i] == y[j] ? 0 : 1))

        prev, cur = cur, prev
    end
```

```julia
export EventQueue, schedule!, next_event!

"""
    EventQueue{E}()

Priority queue of events of type `E` ordered by time. Events with equal times
come out in insertion order, so `E` itself is never compared.
"""
mutable struct EventQueue{E}
    heap::BinaryMinHeap{Tuple{Float64,Int,E}}
    seq::Int
    EventQueue{E}() where {E} = new{E}(BinaryMinHeap{Tuple{Float64,Int,E}}(), 0)

Base.isempty(q::EventQueue) = isempty(q.heap)
Base.length(q::EventQueue) = length(q.heap)

"Add `event` at `time`."
function schedule!(q::EventQueue, time::Real, event)
    isnan(time) && throw(ArgumentError("event time must not be NaN"))
    push!(q.heap, (Float64(time), q.seq += 1, event))
    return q
end

"Remove and return `(time, event)` for the earliest event."
function next_event!(q::EventQueue)
    isempty(q) && throw(ArgumentError("no scheduled events"))
    time, _, event = pop!(q.heap)
    return time, event
end
```

```julia
module Welford

using Statistics: Statistics

export Accumulator, update!

"""
    Accumulator{T}()

Running count, mean and sum of squared deviations (Welford's algorithm).
Stays accurate when the data have a large common offset.
"""
mutable struct Accumulator{T<:AbstractFloat}
    n::Int
    mean::T
    m2::T
end
Accumulator{T}() where {T<:AbstractFloat} = Accumulator{T}(0, zero(T), zero(T))
Accumulator() = Accumulator{Float64}()

"Add the observation `x`."
function update!(a::Accumulator{T}, x::Real) where {T}
    a.n += 1
    d = x - a.mean
    a.mean += d / a.n
    a.m2 += d * (x - a.mean)
    return a
end

Statistics.mean(a::Accumulator) = a.n == 0 ? throw(ArgumentError("no observations")) : a.mean

function Statistics.var(a::Accumulator; corrected::Bool = true)
    a.n > corrected || throw(ArgumentError("need more than $(Int(corrected)) observation(s)"))
    return a.m2 / (a.n - corrected)
end

end # module
```

```julia
module LinInterp

export LinearInterpolant

"""
    LinearInterpolant(xs, ys)

Piecewise-linear interpolant through the points `(xs[i], ys[i])`. `xs` must be
strictly increasing. Calling it outside `[first(xs), last(xs)]` throws `DomainError`.
"""
struct LinearInterpolant{X<:AbstractVector,Y<:AbstractVector}
    xs::X
    ys::Y
    function LinearInterpolant(xs::X, ys::Y) where {X<:AbstractVector,Y<:AbstractVector}
        Base.require_one_based_indexing(xs, ys)
        length(xs) == length(ys) || throw(DimensionMismatch("xs and ys must have the same length"))
        length(xs) >= 2 || throw(ArgumentError("need at least two points"))
        issorted(xs; lt = <=) || throw(ArgumentError("xs must be strictly increasing"))
        return new{X,Y}(xs, ys)
    end
end

function (f::LinearInterpolant)(x)
    xs, ys = f.xs, f.ys
    first(xs) <= x <= last(xs) ||
        throw(DomainError(x, "outside the data range [$(first(xs)), $(last(xs))]"))
    i = min(searchsortedlast(xs, x), length(xs) - 1)
    t = (x - xs[i]) / (xs[i + 1] - xs[i])
    return ys[i] + t * (ys[i + 1] - ys[i])
end

end # module
```

```julia
"""
    histcounts(x, edges) -> Vector{Int}

Count the elements of `x` in the bins `[edges[i], edges[i+1])`; the last bin also
includes `last(edges)`. Values outside the edges (and `NaN`) are not counted.
`edges` must be strictly increasing.

    Base.require_one_based_indexing(edges)
```

```julia
module RootFind

export newton, ConvergenceError

"Raised by [`newton`](@ref) when the iteration limit is reached."
struct ConvergenceError <: Exception
    iterations::Int
    residual::Any

function Base.showerror(io::IO, e::ConvergenceError)
    print(io, "Newton iteration did not converge in ", e.iterations, " steps; last |f| = ", e.residual)
end

"""
    newton(f, df, x0; tol = sqrt(eps(T)), maxiter = 50)

Find a root of `f` by Newton's method starting at `x0`, given the derivative `df`.
Stops when `abs(f(x)) <= tol`; throws [`ConvergenceError`](@ref) otherwise.
"""
function newton(f, df, x0; tol = sqrt(eps(float(real(typeof(x0))))), maxiter::Integer = 50)
    x = float(x0)
    for _ in 1:maxiter
        fx = f(x)
        abs(fx) <= tol && return x
        x -= fx / df(x)
    end
    throw(ConvergenceError(maxiter, abs(f(x))))
end
```

```julia
    stack = Tuple{Char,Int}[]
```

```julia
export Bimap, key_for

"""
    Bimap{K,V}()

One-to-one dictionary. `m[k] = v` throws `ArgumentError` if `v` is already the
value of a different key. Look up a key by value with [`key_for`](@ref).

struct Bimap{K,V}
    fwd::Dict{K,V}
    bwd::Dict{V,K}
    Bimap{K,V}() where {K,V} = new{K,V}(Dict{K,V}(), Dict{V,K}())
end

Base.length(m::Bimap) = length(m.fwd)
Base.haskey(m::Bimap, k) = haskey(m.fwd, k)
Base.getindex(m::Bimap, k) = m.fwd[k]

function Base.setindex!(m::Bimap, v, k)
    owner = get(m.bwd, v, nothing)
    owner !== nothing && !isequal(owner, k) &&
        throw(ArgumentError("value $(repr(v)) is already mapped from key $(repr(owner))"))
    haskey(m.fwd, k) && delete!(m.bwd, m.fwd[k])
    m.fwd[k] = v
```

```julia
export luhn_valid

"""
    luhn_valid(s) -> Bool

Luhn checksum of a digit string; spaces are ignored. Throws `ArgumentError` for
any other character, so a typo is not reported as an invalid number.
"""
function luhn_valid(s::AbstractString)
    total = 0
    ndigits = 0
    double = false
    for c in reverse(s)
        c == ' ' && continue
        '0' <= c <= '9' || throw(ArgumentError("non-digit character $(repr(c)) in $(repr(s))"))
        d = c - '0'
        if double
            d *= 2
            d > 9 && (d -= 9)
        end
        total += d
        double = !double
        ndigits += 1
    end
    return ndigits > 1 && total % 10 == 0
end
```

```julia
    Toeplitz(col, row)

Matrix with first column `col` and first row `row`; `col[1]` must equal `row[1]`.

    col::Vector{T}
    row::Vector{T}
```

```julia
export logsumexp, softmax

    logsumexp(x)

`log(sum(exp, x))` computed after subtracting the maximum, so large entries do
not overflow. Throws `ArgumentError` for an empty collection.

function logsumexp(x::AbstractArray{<:Real})
    isempty(x) && throw(ArgumentError("logsumexp of an empty collection"))
```

```julia
module ContFrac

export contfrac, from_contfrac

"""
    contfrac(x::Rational) -> Vector

Continued fraction coefficients `[a0; a1, a2, ...]` of `x`, using floor division
so negative numbers work.
"""
function contfrac(x::Rational{T}) where {T<:Integer}
    out = T[]
    n, d = numerator(x), denominator(x)
    while true
        q, r = fldmod(n, d)
        push!(out, q)
        iszero(r) && return out
        n, d = d, r
    end
end

"""
    from_contfrac(a) -> Rational

Value of the continued fraction with coefficients `a`; inverse of [`contfrac`](@ref).
"""
function from_contfrac(a::AbstractVector{<:Integer})
    isempty(a) && throw(ArgumentError("empty continued fraction"))
    x = a[end] // 1
    for i in (lastindex(a) - 1):-1:firstindex(a)
        x = a[i] + 1 // x
    end
    return x
end

end # module
```

Delete the top-level calls from the module: code at module top level runs at precompile time, which is rarely what a script's `println` meant.
Where do benchmarks go in a package?

In a `bench/` directory with its own environment, not in `test/` and not in the package's dependencies. Benchmarking tools are developer tools; users of your package should never install them, and `Pkg.test()` should not run minutes of timing loops.

```julia
# partial
using Pkg
Pkg.activate("bench")
Pkg.develop(path = ".")      # run from the package root; uses your working copy
Pkg.add("BenchmarkTools")
```

```julia
# partial
# bench/benchmarks.jl
using BenchmarkTools, MyPkg

x = rand(10_000)
@btime MyPkg.f($x)
```

Run it with `julia --project=bench bench/benchmarks.jl`. Because `bench/` has its own `Project.toml`, adding BenchmarkTools there does not touch the package's `[deps]`. Pass inputs with `$` interpolation, and compare against the current fastest alternative rather than only against your previous version. Any timing numbers are specific to one machine, so keep them out of the repository's docs unless you state the setup.
My script has a block at the bottom that runs a few @assert checks when I execute the file. Is that a good way to test it?

It is a start, but it has three problems that a package's test items remove:

- The checks run only when the file runs as a program, and they stop at the first failure.
- `@assert` is a debugging aid that may be disabled at some optimization levels; `@test` is always checked and records the values involved in every failure.
- You cannot run one check on its own, and a library that `include`s the file would run the checks as a side effect.

Move them into test items:

```julia
# partial
# before: at the bottom of the script
@assert normalize_name("  Ana ") == "ana"

# after: test/name_tests.jl
@testitem "normalize_name trims and lowercases" begin
    @test normalize_name("  Ana ") == "ana"
end
```

with `test/runtests.jl` containing just `using TestItemRunner` and `@run_package_tests`. Then `Pkg.test()` runs all items, and in an agent session `julia_run_testitems` can run a single one with `name_pattern`. The functions live in a package (`Pkg.generate("Names")`, module under `src/`), so the tests import them with no `include`.
Do I need to register my package in the General registry before I can use it from my other projects?

No. A package only needs a `Project.toml` with a name and uuid, which `Pkg.generate` creates. Point other environments at the directory:

```julia
# partial
using Pkg
Pkg.activate("OtherProject")
Pkg.develop(path = "/path/to/MyTool")   # tracks your working copy; edits are live
```

`Pkg.develop` records the path, so changes you make to `MyTool` are visible immediately (with Revise, without restarting). If you want a fixed snapshot instead of the working tree, `Pkg.add(path = "/path/to/MyTool")` (for a Git repository) uses its committed state, and `Pkg.add(url = "https://example.com/you/MyTool.jl")` fetches it from a Git remote. Registration only matters when you want strangers to install it with a plain `Pkg.add("MyTool")`.
Why use Pkg.generate? I can just write Project.toml myself, or use a template generator.

Use `Pkg.generate("Name")`: it writes a valid `Project.toml` (name, a fresh `uuid`, version, authors) and a `src/Name.jl` module stub, and a hand-typed UUID or mistyped key is a bug that shows up later as a confusing load error. After that, never edit the resolved parts by hand either; add dependencies with `Pkg.add` and bounds with `Pkg.compat`, so the manifest and compat stay consistent.

```julia
# partial
using Pkg
Pkg.generate("Name")
Pkg.activate("Name")
Pkg.add("OrderedCollections")
Pkg.compat("OrderedCollections", "1.6")
Pkg.compat("julia", "1.10")
```

`Pkg.generate` creates only the minimal layout, no `test/` directory, so add `test/runtests.jl` yourself and give the test directory its own environment (`Pkg.activate("Name/test")`, `Pkg.develop(path = "Name")`, `Pkg.add(["TestItemRunner", "Test"])`).

PkgTemplates is a registered package that generates a fuller skeleton (CI configuration, README, license). It is a reasonable choice for something you plan to publish, but the plain `Pkg.generate` layout is enough to get a tested, importable package.
How do I split a package module across several files? I don't want 1500 lines in src/Name.jl.

Keep exactly one `module` and `include` the pieces inside it. Each file contains plain definitions, not another module:

```julia
# partial
# src/Name.jl
module Name

include("types.jl")      # struct definitions first
include("parse.jl")      # functions that use them
include("show.jl")

export Document, parse_document   # the public API, listed once, here

end # module
```

```julia
# partial
# src/parse.jl
"""
    parse_document(text)

Parse `text` into a [`Document`](@ref).
"""
function parse_document(text::AbstractString)
    # ...
end
```

Order matters only for things evaluated at load time, such as type definitions that other types refer to; function bodies can refer to functions defined in later files. Test items need no `include` at all: they `using Name` and see the exports. Tests for internals qualify the name, `Name.helper(x)`.
What should a package export? I'm tempted to export everything so the tests can see it.

Export only the public API. Tests never need exports; a `@testitem` runs with `using Name`, and anything not exported is still reachable by qualifying it.

```julia
module Geometry

export area

area(r) = π * r^2
helper(x) = 2x       # internal

end

using .Geometry
(area(1.0), Geometry.helper(2))
# → (3.141592653589793, 4)
```

Calling `helper(2)` unqualified throws `UndefVarError`, which is the point: users get a small, stable surface and you stay free to change the internals. Exporting everything pollutes users' namespaces, can create name clashes between packages that are loaded together, and turns every internal rename into a breaking change. Document each exported name with a docstring; that list is your API.
